title: StableStaker deployed with pauser == address(0): farm has no working emergency stop and is excluded from the global Pauser
description: Phase 3.7 deploys + wires StableStaker but never calls setPauser, and Phase 8 (Pauser Registration) wires setPauser + pauser.register for every other IPausable protocol contract (PhusdStableMinter, PhlimboEA, StableYieldAccumulator, NFTMinter, NFTMinterV2, NFTStaker — 6 setPauser + 6 register calls, source lines 810-846) while OMITTING StableStaker entirely. Empirically StableStaker.pauser() == address(0). StableStaker.pause() is onlyPauser (require msg.sender == pauser); with pauser == address(0) no caller can satisfy it — confirmed: `cast send pause()` as the owner reverts 'StableStaker: only pauser'. The contract can therefore NEVER be paused, the whenNotPaused guard on stake/withdraw/claim is dead, and the global EYE-burn Pauser trigger skips StableStaker because it was never registered.
impact: The StableStaker farm has no functioning emergency-stop in this deployment: neither a direct pause() nor the ecosystem-wide global Pauser can halt stake/withdraw/claim during an incident, even though every sibling protocol contract can. Deviation from the deployment's own established Phase-8 pattern for pausable contracts. On anvil this is local-only; the finding's value is that the same DeployMocks Phase-3.7/Phase-8 omission would carry to any environment cloned from this script.
evidence: dev/side-effects.json: pauser()=0x0; negativeTest pause()->'StableStaker: only pauser'; source enumeration shows 6 register()/6 setPauser() calls, none for stableStaker. StableStaker not present in Pauser registry.
recommendation: In Phase 3.7 (or Phase 8 alongside the other contracts) call stableStaker.setPauser(address(pauser)) and pauser.register(address(stableStaker)), following the same 'setPauser BEFORE register' ordering used for the other six contracts.

title: StableStaker deployed with migrator == address(0): terminal-migration path is permanently unreachable
description: Phase 3.7 never calls setMigrator, so StableStaker.migrator() == address(0) (confirmed via cast). initiateMigration/batchMigrate/depositFor are onlyMigrator (require msg.sender == migrator); with migrator == address(0) none are reachable, so the terminal-migration escape hatch and the StableStakerMigrator orchestrator are inert in this deployment. Healthy-path withdraw/emergencyWithdraw do NOT depend on migrator — _routeExit/withdraw routing is migrator-independent (read of StableStaker.sol withdraw/_routeExit confirms migrator is referenced only by the migration entrypoints), so normal exits are unaffected (verify run withdrew principal cleanly).
impact: No incident-response migration is possible for the dev StableStaker (e.g. moving stakers to a new staker if a strategy winds down). Lower severity than the pauser gap because (a) it does not affect any healthy user path and (b) it can be set post-deploy by the owner at any time. Recorded as a half-configured deployment consistent with the deployment's stated optional-wiring step.
evidence: dev/side-effects.json: migrator()=0x0; StableStaker.sol onlyMigrator modifier gates initiateMigration/batchMigrate/depositFor; withdraw()/emergencyWithdraw()/_routeExit() contain no migrator reference.
recommendation: If the dev flow is meant to exercise migration, deploy StableStakerMigrator and call stableStaker.setMigrator(migrator) in Phase 3.7. Otherwise document explicitly that migration is intentionally out of scope for local dev.

title: verify-stable-staker.sh relies on ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY from .envrc but never exports it — npm test:stable-staker fails on a fresh clone / CI
description: verify-stable-staker.sh hardcodes and exports PRIVATE_KEY (anvil acct0) but the interaction scripts StakeStableStaker.s.sol and ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol read vm.envUint("ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY") — a DIFFERENT variable the shell never exports. The flow only works because the repo-root .envrc (direnv) sets ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY in the ambient shell. Confirmed empirically: with .envrc sourced the full flow passes green; with ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY unset (env -u, keeping PRIVATE_KEY set as the shell would) STEP 1 reverts immediately: 'vm.envUint: environment variable "ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY" not found'.
impact: The advertised one-command verification (npm run test:stable-staker) is not self-contained: any developer cloning fresh, or any CI runner, that does not load the repo-root .envrc gets an immediate revert in STEP 1 before any staking — the smoke check cannot run. The script exports the wrong variable name, so the PRIVATE_KEY it does set is never consumed.
evidence: verify-stable-staker/side-effects.json negativeTest: revertReason 'vm.envUint: environment variable "ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY" not found'. Shell exports PRIVATE_KEY (line 21) not ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY; scripts read ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY (StakeStableStaker.s.sol:33, ClaimWithdrawStableStaker.s.sol:29).
recommendation: Either export ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY in verify-stable-staker.sh (export ANVIL_PRIVATE_KEY="$PRIVATE_KEY"), or change the interaction scripts to read PRIVATE_KEY. Aligning the names removes the hidden .envrc dependency and makes the smoke check runnable from a clean checkout / CI.

title: ClaimWithdrawStableStaker reward assertion lower band (9.9 phUSD) is loose enough to mask a materially wrong emission rate
description: The verification asserts rewardCredited in [9.9e18, 10.1e18] (EXPECTED_DAILY_PHUSD ±1%). The realized reward is 9999999999999936000 — only 64000 wei (6.4e-15 of 10e18) short of the 10e18 ideal, because phusdPerSecond = floor(10e18/86400) loses 64000 wei/day. The actual flooring dust is ~9 orders of magnitude smaller than the 1e17 (1%) band. The wide band is therefore a smoke-only tolerance: it would still pass if the deploy-set rate were off by up to ~1% (e.g. a config typo setting 9.95e18/day or an off-by-one in the per-second conversion). For a script whose stated purpose is to VERIFY the 10-vs-5 phUSD/day config split, a ±1% band on the rate it is verifying is weaker than the data supports.
impact: Smoke check only — it confirms reward accrues at roughly the right magnitude, not that the rate is exactly the configured 10 phUSD/day. A future deploy-config drift within 1% would pass verification silently. No funds impact; this is a test-strength / spec-fidelity observation on a verification script.
evidence: verify-stable-staker/side-effects.json realizedValues: rewardCredited 9999999999999936000, perDayFloorLoss_wei 64000, asserted band [9.9e18,10.1e18]. STEP 1 already exact-asserts phusdPerSecond == 10 ether/86400, so the rate itself is checked there; the reward-band check adds little beyond 'time advanced'.
recommendation: Tighten the reward band toward the actual dust (e.g. assert rewardCredited within a few thousand wei of 86400*phusdPerSecond using the on-chain phusdPerSecond, not a hardcoded 10e18 ±1%). The STEP-1 exact rate assert is the real config guard; the band is redundant and overly loose.
